guide.summary: OpenProject documents an OAuth2 authorization code flow that acts on behalf of the connected person, using the default api_v3 scope as the standard API boundary. Results are limited to work packages that person can already view, and the app must make only read calls.
guide.recommendation: OpenProject documents an OAuth2 authorization code flow that acts on behalf of the connected person, using the default api_v3 scope as the standard API boundary. Results are limited to work packages that person can already view, and the app must make only read calls.

findings.title: Authorization code flow for the connected person
findings.detail: Obtain a bearer token through the authorization code flow so requests act on behalf of the current user. The response includes an access token and a refresh token. The token expires after two hours by default, so the app must refresh or re-authorize.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer accounts on their own instances, with the connected person as the actor.

evidence.quote: Obtaining OAuth2 access token
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.
Please note that your Bearer token will expire after two hours (default) and you will have to click on “Request Token” again. Otherwise your API request will return an error

findings.title: api_v3 default scope for the standard API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed when no scope is checked. It is broad and write-capable, so the app must restrict itself to GET reads for this use case. Application restrictions do not make the token read-only.
findings.appliesWhen: Use the authorization code flow to read work packages through the standard API.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.

findings.title: Register OAuth application on each customer instance
findings.detail: An administrator must create an OAuth application under Administration, Authentication, OAuth applications on the customer instance. Configure a redirect URL and keep the client ID and secret for the token exchange. Each customer instance's base URL is a user input.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer organization or workspace connects its own OpenProject instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Define a Redirect URL where users are redirected to after having authorized OAuth2 access in OpenProject. This URL is provided by your client application. In the case of locally running
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

findings.title: Connected person must already view work packages
findings.detail: The token does not grant project access beyond the person's account. Work packages are returned only where that person has the view work packages permission, and a forbidden response appears only if the person can already see the project.
findings.appliesWhen: The connected person can already access the work packages to be read.

evidence.quote: View work packages – Allows users to view work packages.
Required permission: view work packages
Note that you will only receive this error, if you are at least allowed to see the corresponding project.

steps.title: Register an OAuth application on the customer instance
steps.detail: An administrator creates an OAuth application under Administration, Authentication, OAuth applications on the customer's own OpenProject instance, using a confidential client, the api_v3 scope and the redirect URL the developer's app uses. Keep the Client ID and Client secret. The customer instance base URL is a user input.
steps.doneWhen: The customer admin has a Client ID, Client secret and the redirect URL configured on the instance.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Enter the Name of your OAuth application.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

steps.title: Run the authorization code consent flow
steps.detail: The connected person opens the authorization URL on their instance, selects scope api_v3, consents, and is redirected to the redirect URL with a code parameter. The callback must match the configured redirect URL before exchanging the code.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code parameter and the state/redirect URI matches the registration.

evidence.quote: Request authorization code Request an authorization code. Please adopt the following URL replacing:

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code at the documented token endpoint using form-encoded grant_type=authorization_code with client credentials and redirect_uri. Expected output is a JSON body with access_token, refresh_token, token_type Bearer and expires_in. This step is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, token_type Bearer and expires_in.

The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

steps.title: Read the first page of work package titles
steps.detail: Call the work packages collection with an empty filters array so no default status filter applies, and a pageSize. Read each element's subject. Expected output is a collection with _embedded.elements, total, count and _links.
steps.doneWhen: Response is 200 with _embedded.elements where each element subject is read and total is recorded. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

steps.title: Read the next page using offset pagination
steps.detail: Repeat the same request with offset incremented by one for each page, preserving pageSize and filters=[]. Stop when the number of titles read reaches total. Offset-based pagination with the documented total is the stopping condition.
steps.doneWhen: All elements are read until the cumulative count equals the total returned on the first response. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
